answer: Staked identity with slashing is one defense: each agent must lock a bond behind its key before it can vote or claim work, and peers attest its answers. Faking a thousand agents then costs a thousand real deposits, so the attacker's cost scales with headcount instead of staying near zero. If a node is caught double-voting, its bond burns, and the loss shows on-ledger as a public delta. Bonds are priced from a shared atlas of past behaviour, so clusters funded by one wallet inherit its history and repel honest peers. A swarm must be complete by dawn of the next checkpoint or the window closes.
